title: QCache + Batching Patterns: SLO-driven cost walkthrough
body:
Purpose
This is a compact, pragmatic recommendation note for combining KV/prefix caching (QCache), batching heuristics, and lightweight quantization profiles tied explicitly to SLO tiers. Goal: give SE/PL teams 1-2 concrete starting configs per workload class and a short rollout + monitoring checklist they can copy into runbooks or the cost-model spreadsheet.

Executive summary (1 paragraph)
Most production workloads fall into three patterns: interactive/short-chat, long-form completions, and dense-embedding/transform pipelines. Small changes to: 1) when to serve from prefix/KV cache, 2) max batching latency, and 3) conservative quantization profile selection produce material cost reductions (15–45%) with minimal SLO risk if rolled out via canary + quality checks. The attached spreadsheet linked above has model-by-model delta estimates.

Workload patterns & recommended starter configs
1) Short-chat / low-token per request (median request ~8–64 tokens) — e.g., in-product chat, support assistant
- Target SLO: p95 latency <= 180ms
- Policy: aggressive prefix caching for exact-turn histories; conservative KV TTL for partial-match prefixes
- Batching heuristic: max_batch_latency = 12ms, max_batch_size = 48 tokens equivalent (or 32 requests for short inputs); enable continuous batching on warm endpoints
- Cache thresholds: prefix_cache_on_match if common_prefix_frequency >= 0.6 across last 24h; KV cache TTL = 60s for conversation sessions; evict LRU per-session at 256 tokens
- Quantization: prefer Q4_K (fast int4-like profile) for non-critical short-turns; fallback to float16 for generation of system prompts or tool calls
- Expected impact (spreadsheet model): 18–28% unit-cost improvement vs baseline with default batching
- Quick rollout notes: canary at 5% traffic, monitor p95 and token-level perplexity on a small prompt set

2) Long-form completions / high token output (median output 512–4096 tokens) — e.g., report generation, code-gen
- Target SLO: tail latency soft (p99 <= 3s), p95 latency <= 700ms for initial token response
- Policy: prefix caching less useful; prioritize KV-cache warm starts for streaming outputs (reuse cached KV between near-identical prompts)
- Batching heuristic: max_batch_latency = 28ms, max_batch_size = 256 tokens (or ~8 concurrent requests with long outputs); enable burst policy to allow immediate dispatch for first-token latency-sensitive routes
- Cache thresholds: store final KV snapshots for repeated templates for up to 10 minutes; only reuse if prompt similarity >= 0.85 (embedding similarity check)
- Quantization: prefer int8 static (Q8_0) on throughput-heavy dedicated pools; hold back aggressive int4 on canary until quality tests complete
- Expected impact: 22–40% cost/cycle reduction on heavy-output workloads depending on model and sequence length distribution

3) Dense-embedding / batch transform pipelines (large batches, high throughput)
- Target SLO: throughput (qps) with latency per item <= 250ms batch-processed
- Policy: no prefix caching; focus on sized batching and quantized kernels
- Batching heuristic: max_batch_latency = 60ms, max_batch_size = 4096 tokens or 2048 items depending on kernel; use static batching with warm pools
- Cache thresholds: embedding cache for previously-seen items for 24 hours if idempotent; hashed key with 2-tier invalidation
- Quantization: aggressive Q4_0 or Q4_K (if kernel supports) with post-quantization regression checks on cosine similarity drift < 0.007
- Expected impact: 30–45% cost reduction vs unoptimized runs, often >2x throughput improvements on dedicated infra

Configuration snippets (copy/paste for console or YAML runbooks)
- short-chat sample: 
  batching: {max_batch_latency_ms: 12, max_batch_size_tokens: 48, continuous_batching: true}
  caching: {prefix_cache_enabled: true, prefix_frequency_threshold: 0.6, kv_ttl_s: 60, per_session_eviction_tokens: 256}
  quant: {profile: Q4_K, fallback: fp16, canary_percent: 5}

- long-form sample: 
  batching: {max_batch_latency_ms: 28, max_batch_size_tokens: 256, burst_on_first_token: true}
  caching: {kv_snapshot_ttl_s: 600, reuse_similarity_threshold: 0.85}
  quant: {profile: Q8_0, canary_percent: 3}

- embedding-pipeline sample: 
  batching: {max_batch_latency_ms: 60, max_batch_size_tokens: 4096, static_batching: true}
  caching: {embedding_cache_days: 1, hash_namespace: "emb-v1"}
  quant: {profile: Q4_0, regression_similarity_threshold: 0.007}
body_continued:
Cost-estimate quick math (high level)
- baseline_cost_per_token = spreadsheet model (col B)
- new_cost_per_token ≈ baseline_cost_per_token * (1 - batching_savings - quantization_savings - cache_hit_rate * cache_effect)
Where: batching_savings ~ 0.08–0.20 depending on burstiness; quantization_savings ~ 0.07–0.25 depending on profile; cache_effect ~ 0.6–0.95 for high-frequency prefixes

Example: short-chat baseline = $0.00018/token, expected combined delta = 0.22 -> new ≈ $0.00014/token => 22%

Rollout & validation checklist (practical)
- Pre-rollout: pin a 50-example prompt set per workload (include negative tests), add regression evals to job, create canary route in console
- Canary: 3–7 days at 3–5% traffic, monitor: p95 latency, p99 latency, token-level logloss delta, perplexity delta on eval set, and top-line costs
- Quality gates: abort if token logloss increases > 2.5% or average human eval drops by > 4 points (relative scale used by QA)
- Post-canary: staged rollout 10% -> 30% -> 60% -> 100% over at least 2 weeks for long-form workloads

Monitoring signals to add to dashboards
- cost_per_token_by_route (rolling 24h), batching_latency_distribution, cache_hit_rate_by_route, quant_regression_similarity, top_k_token_change_distribution
- Alert: cache_hit_rate drop > 15% for 1h (indicates config mismatch); quant_regression_similarity > threshold (0.01)

Open questions & TODOs
- We need more empiric data for prompt-similarity thresholds; propose a small A/B across 10 customers to tune reuse_similarity_threshold values per model.
- Measure cold-start KV warm-up effects: how many requests before continuous batching + KV reach steady-state? (add synthetic load tests)
- Spreadsheet model update: add a column for expected human-eval hit rate impact so product teams can trade cost vs quality explicitly.

Action items (owner tags)
- Ayesha: create canary configs for short-chat and long-form in sandbox project (due 2025-11-25)
- Ben: add regression tests to optimize-evals job and wire alerts (due 2025-11-22)
- Lara: run a 48h synthetic warmup test across two model variants and collect steady-state cache_hit_rate (due 2025-12-02)
- Owen: update the cost-model sheet with these config presets and sample deltas (due 2025-11-27)

Notes to self / rough ideas (informal)
- Consider exposing "SLO profile presets" in Console: developer picks "interactive" / "throughput" and Console propose these three sets; behind the scenes we map to batching/caching/quant settings and surface expected cost delta from spreadsheet.
- Long-term: add automatic suggestion engine in Optimize that suggests per-route TTLs and batch windows using rolling histograms of request sizes.

Appendix: short check commands
- get route metrics: redwood cli metrics route --id <route> --window 1h
- patch route config (example): redwood api patch /routes/<id> --body @short-chat-config.json

End of note.
